dialog.body: Public Works, this is Denise, how can I help you?
Hi, yeah, Denise. My name's Walter Sisson. I'm calling about water coming out of a pipe at the curb, and it's turning the sidewalk into a skating rink. Which, in January, is just great.
Oh no. Okay, where is this, Walter?

472 Eustis Avenue, up on the Hill. Right at the curb in front of it there's a pipe, and water just runs out of it all day. No rain, no snow melting, nothing. It's dry out. So where's it coming from, right? Somebody ought to know that.
Okay, 472 Eustis. And it's running right now?

Right now. I'm standing here looking at it. I'm on foot, I've got a backpack on that weighs about forty pounds, and I'm waiting to cross the street, and I'm not crossing on that ice, I'll tell you that. The whole sidewalk is a sheet. Somebody's going to go down and break a hip.
Yeah, that's not good. Is it a steady stream or more of a trickle?

Steady. Not a gush, but steady. It runs across the sidewalk, down toward the corner, and freezes as it goes. By the time it hits the walkway it's solid. Clear ice, too, which is the worst kind because you can't even see it.
Right, black ice. Is the pipe sticking out of a wall, or is it a opening in the curb itself?
It's an opening in the curb, kind of a pipe end poking out of the stone. Looks like it drains from somewhere uphill. Which, fine, I get that, but it never did this much before.
So it's happened before, just not as much?

Last winter there was a little dampness there, a wet patch, maybe a little ice at the edge. Nothing like this. This year it's a glacier. So something changed, and I'd bet money it's a broken line somewhere, but that's your department's guess to make, not mine.
Fair enough. I'll write all of that down. Let me get the details in the request. Can I get a callback number?
Got it, 401-555-0197. And Walter, you said it's dry weather, no storm lately?
Nothing. Last real snow was ages ago. It's been cold and dry for days. That's why this makes no sense. If it were runoff, okay, but this is just a constant flow.
Okay. That points to something other than regular storm runoff, so it may go to a different crew, maybe water or sewer side. I'll flag it so they look at it.
Okay, good. And can you tell me when they last came by? Because if somebody checked this out recently and missed it, I'd like to know. If nobody's been out at all, I'd like to know that too.
Let me look at the address history. [pause] Bear with me, the system's slow today.
Take your time. I'm not going anywhere. I mean I'd love to go somewhere, but not over this ice.
Okay. I'm seeing an older note on that drain, but I can't tell from here exactly what the crew did. It doesn't show a visit this winter. I can tell you that much.
So nobody's been out this winter. That's what I figured. Wonderful. So it's been like this for who knows how long and it's not even on anyone's list.
It's on the list now. I'm marking it as an icing hazard on a public sidewalk, which gets it looked at sooner than a regular drainage request.
Good, because that's what it is. A hazard. Can anybody at least throw some salt or sand on it in the meantime?
I'll put that in the notes, asking for salt or sand as a first step. I can't promise what time they'll get there, but I'll send it over to the crew supervisor right after we hang up.
Okay. Do you have a sense of today, tomorrow, next week? Because kids walk this sidewalk to school.

Hazard calls usually get priority, so I'd hope today or tomorrow, but I don't want to hand you a time I can't back up. If it gets worse or somebody falls, call us back right away, and if it's an emergency, call 911.
Alright. I'll walk around on the other side. Just, honestly, I wish somebody had caught this earlier. Anyone walking by could have told you it was freezing over.

I hear you, and I'm sorry. Thanks for calling it in. Let me read it back. 472 Eustis Avenue, water running from a curb pipe in dry weather, icing across the sidewalk, worse than last winter, callback 401-555-0197. Right?
That's it. That's everything.
Okay, Walter. It's in. Be careful crossing.
Will do. Thanks, Denise.
You're welcome. Bye now.
